newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss aid Belgium in Credit Lyonnais fraud probe.
newsitem.headline: Swiss aid Belgium in Credit Lyonnais fraud probe.

text.p: A Swiss judge said on Tuesday that he had begun an inquiry into possible money-laundering in connection with 3.5 billion Belgian francs ($100 million) allegedly stolen by a former employee of Credit Lyonnais Belgium SA and her husband.

Jacques Antenen, investigating magistrate in Lausanne for Vaud canton (state), said he had ordered searches last weekend of the home and business offices of the woman's husband in the resort of Villars-sur-Ollon.

The woman, a long-time employee of Credit Lyonnais Belgium SA's office in Ghent, was arrested last week on charges of theft and forgery. Her businessman husband was also arrested on suspicion of having received stolen goods.
Neither have been formally charged in what appears to be the largest Belgian bank fraud ever. Credit Lyonnais Belgium SA said last Friday it was the victim of an international fraud ring.
"I have opened an inquiry, based on information given by Credit Lyonnais, which I consider to be a complement to the investigation in Belgium," Antenen told Reuters.
In their request for judicial assistance, received on Monday, Belgian authorities also referred to possible criminal activity in the Swiss canton of Jura, according to the judge.
Antenen said he was checking whether people in Villars who collaborated with the husband "knew the origin of the money."
"Certain questions can be raised legitimately as to the origin of these funds -- 'dirty money' generated by fraud," the judge added.
"I ordered a search of all the places which I knew of which may bring interesting elements, his home and business offices... "I confirm I ordered a search of Vilmont Investissement SA."
Antenen said he expected to hear witnesses and request more documents in connection with the case. ($ = 34.88 Belgian Francs)
